front: Which class of organic compounds contains the –COOH group?
back: Carboxylic acids.

front: Which class of organic compounds contains an –OH group bonded to a saturated carbon atom?
back: Alcohols.

front: Which class of organic compounds contains the –C≡N group?
back: Nitriles. The carbon of the –C≡N group is bonded to the rest of the molecule.

front: Which class of organic compounds contains an –NH₂ group bonded to an alkyl group?
back: Primary amines.

front: What is the name of the –CH₃ group?
back: Methyl. It is an alkyl substituent, rather than a functional group.

front: What is the condensed structural formula of propane?
back: CH₃CH₂CH₃

front: What is the molecular formula of an acyclic hexene with one C=C bond?
back: C₆H₁₂

front: What naming suffix is used for a carboxylic acid?
back:
Suffix: -oic acid
Example: propanoic acid.

front: What ending is used for the acid-derived part of an ester’s name?
back:
Suffix: -oate
Example: ethyl propanoate. The alkyl group bonded to oxygen is named first.

front: What prefix and suffix can be used for an alcohol group?
back:
Prefix: hydroxy-
Suffix: -ol
Use hydroxy- when the –OH group is named as a substituent because a higher-priority group supplies the suffix.

front: How is an ester linkage written using R-group notation?
back:
R–C(=O)–O–R′
The carbonyl carbon is bonded directly to O–R′. The groups on the two sides need not be the same.

front: Which class of organic compounds has the general structure R–O–R′?
back: Ethers.

front: How does the bonding at the carbonyl group differ in an aldehyde and a ketone?
back:
Aldehyde: the carbonyl carbon is bonded to at least one hydrogen, giving a –CHO group.
Ketone: the carbonyl carbon is bonded to two carbon atoms, giving R–C(=O)–R′.

front: What is the functional group of an alkene?
back: A carbon–carbon double bond, C=C.

front: What type of carbon–carbon bonds are present in alkanes?
back: Single covalent bonds only.

front: What functional group is shared by aldehydes and ketones?
back: The carbonyl group, C=O.

front: What naming suffix is used for a ketone?
back:
Suffix: -one
Example: propanone.

front: What naming suffix is used for an aldehyde?
back:
Suffix: -al
Example: methanal.

front: In the ester name ethyl propanoate, which part identifies the carboxylic acid from which it is derived?
back:
Propanoate identifies the acid-derived part; it is derived from propanoic acid.
Ethyl identifies the alkyl group bonded to the ester oxygen.

front: What is a functional group?
back: An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic chemical reactions of an organic compound.

front: What is a homologous series?
back: A family of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, similar chemical properties, and successive members differing by CH₂.

front: What does a displayed formula show?
back: All the atoms and all the bonds between them. It does not necessarily show the molecule’s actual three-dimensional shape.

front: How do you choose the numbering direction for a simple branched alkane?
back: Number the parent chain to give substituents the lowest set of locants. Compare the possible sets at the first point of difference; do not simply choose the smallest total.

front: How is the parent chain chosen when naming a simple branched alkane?
back: Choose the longest continuous carbon chain. Its number of carbon atoms determines the stem of the name.

front: What does R represent in an organic formula?
back: An unspecified organic group, usually an alkyl group. R and R′ can represent different groups.

front: What is an alkyl group?
back:
A group formed by removing one hydrogen atom from an alkane.
Examples: methyl, –CH₃; ethyl, –CH₂CH₃.

front: What is a haloalkane?
back: A compound derived from an alkane by replacing one or more hydrogen atoms with halogen atoms.

front: Which class of organic compounds contains the –C(=O)Cl group?
back: Acyl chlorides. The chlorine atom is bonded directly to the carbonyl carbon.

front: What is the simplest saturated, acyclic hydrocarbon homologous series?
back: Alkanes.

front: What naming ending is used for an acyl chloride?
back:
Suffix: -oyl chloride
Example: ethanoyl chloride.

front: What is a general formula?
back:
An algebraic formula describing members of a homologous series.
Example: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for acyclic alkanes.

front: What is an empirical formula?
back: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.

front: What is a molecular formula?
back: The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule.

front: What is a structural formula?
back:
A formula showing the arrangement of atoms or groups in a molecule without displaying every bond.
Example: CH₃CH₂CH₃ for propane.
